fields.meta_title: Employee Satisfaction Survey, Scored by Topic | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an employee satisfaction survey that scores pay and workload by site and shift, with confidential results. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an Employee Satisfaction Survey Scored by Topic
fields.hero_description: Name who works for you and what you want rated. Emergent builds the questions, scores each topic by site and shift, and keeps every response in a database you own.
fields.features_subheading: One prompt that names your topics and sites gives your employee satisfaction survey every piece below.
fields.feature_1:
One statement per part of the job

Emergent writes a satisfaction item for each topic you name, such as pay, benefits or your schedule. Add a topic later and it gets an item in the survey and a row in the results.
fields.feature_2:
Percent satisfied for every topic

Each topic is scored as the share of people who chose 4 or 5 on a 1-5 scale. The average sits underneath it, since a split team and a lukewarm team can end up with the same average.
fields.feature_3:
Response rates by site while it runs

The dashboard counts answers by site and shift from the day the survey opens. When one night shift is lagging halfway through, its manager still has time to ask people to fill it in.
fields.feature_4:
Results split by site and shift

Upload a roster with each person's site and shift, or sync it from your HRIS by API. The survey never asks where or when anyone works. Each answer is matched to the roster.
fields.feature_5:
A follow-up only after a low score

When someone answers 1 or 2 on a topic, one open question asks what would change their rating. Each comment is tagged to its topic and listed beside that topic's score in results.
fields.feature_6:
Your survey as code in GitHub

Export the survey, its response tables and its dashboards to your own GitHub repository. Run it on your own servers, edit the code by hand or keep prompting Emergent for changes.
fields.why_description: These tools price per user or per employee and keep responses on their platform. Emergent builds your survey as an app you own.

fields.tab_content_1:
Pay finishes last of seven topics

A 30-question survey on seven topics goes to all 350 employees and stays open for 10 days. Pay comes in last, and the comments under it repeat one complaint: annual raises trail what new hires are offered.
fields.tab_content_2:
Night shift gets its own staffing score

Nurses on every unit answer a nurse satisfaction survey of 18 questions on staffing, scheduling and patient load. Results split by unit and by day or night shift. When fewer than half of one shift on a unit are satisfied with staffing, the unit's nurse manager gets an email with the counts and comments.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each principal reads only their own school

One teacher satisfaction survey link goes to teachers and support staff at nine schools in the district. Each principal sees their own school's results and nothing else, while the district office sees all nine. A school with fewer than five answers shows no results. Planning time scores lowest across the district.
fields.tab_content_4:
Remote and office staff, side by side

Remote and office staff answer the same 12 work satisfaction survey questions about their workspace and equipment. The dashboard puts the two groups in adjacent columns. Remote staff rate home equipment lowest, and their comments become a request list for the IT lead, most asked first.

fields.howto_title: How to Run a Satisfaction Survey
fields.howto_description: Three of these steps happen before you open Emergent, and the last two after the survey closes.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the topics you can change
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the parts of the job leadership can act on this year: pay bands, benefits, schedules, tools, manager training. Leave out what you cannot touch. Asking about something you will not change tells people their answers go nowhere.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Use statements such as "I am satisfied with my pay for the work I do" on a five-point scale that runs from dissatisfied to satisfied. Add one overall item on the job as a whole, and keep open questions to two at most.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Confidential means the system can link answers to people for reminders and team splits. Anonymous means it stores no identity, and every reminder goes to everyone. Say which one it is on the first screen.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Say who gets the survey, which topics it covers and how long it stays open, and include the privacy rule. Emergent builds the survey with its response table and dashboards from that description.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send the draft to a team of 10 or 15 people first and note how long it takes them. Read their comments for questions people misread or skipped, and fix that wording before the company-wide launch.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Sort topics by percent satisfied and begin at the bottom. Open the comments under each low topic, then compare groups. A score that is low on one shift or at one site usually needs a local fix, not a new policy.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Name one change per low topic
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish company results within a few weeks of closing. For the two lowest topics, name one change each and give it an owner. Next year, run the same items with the same wording to see whether those scores moved.

plan.angle: The top 10 is question lists (HRMorning, Voxco, easy-feedback) and fixed templates (SurveyMonkey, SurveyHero, BlockSurvey, Honestly). claims_to_source: Job satisfaction measures how content people are with the job and its conditions, while engagement measures commitment and discretionary effort
Spector's Job Satisfaction Survey has 36 items across nine facets, including pay, promotion, supervision, benefits and coworkers, on a six-point agreement scale
A top-box or percent-favorable score is the share of answers in the top two points of the scale
A confidential survey links answers to identity while an anonymous survey stores no identity
Survey tools hide results for groups below a minimum number of answers
Survey platforms such as Qualtrics log IP address and location with responses unless an anonymize setting is on
Double-barreled questions that ask about two things at once are hard to answer and interpret

scope.evidence: H1 "Build an Employee Satisfaction Survey Scored by Topic"; hero "Emergent builds the questions, scores each topic by site and shift". Contentment by topic, per the watch-list split from the engagement sibling.

intent.evidence: All 7 eligible PAA questions answered; question examples (FAQ 3, 6), template (FAQ 2), scoring (FAQ 5), anonymity (FAQ 4), seven-step how-to; meta promise "scores pay and workload by site and shift, with confidential results" delivered in features 2-4 and step 3.

specificity.evidence: Percent satisfied as 4 or 5 on a 1-5 scale, roster upload or HRIS sync, nurse units by day and night shift, principals limited to their own school, five-answer minimum; table rows on per-user and per-employee pricing.

openers.evidence: features_subheading is now a full sentence: "One prompt that names your topics and sites gives your employee satisfaction survey every piece below." Tabs open on full sentences ("A 30-question survey on seven topics goes to all 350 employees").

craft.evidence: No QC Q5-Q8 hits; one idea per sentence ("Leave out what you cannot touch."); the prompt-pitch echo across hero, features_subheading and step 4 is noted.

voice.evidence: Concrete, unglamorous detail: "annual raises trail what new hires are offered", "who was on shift at 2 a.m.", "My manager keeps Friday afternoons free of meetings."

truth.evidence: feature_4 privacy claim removed ("The survey never asks where or when anyone works. Each answer is matched to the roster."); Spector JSS, top-box, confidential vs anonymous, Qualtrics anonymize, Culture Amp minimum group, Gallup satisfaction vs engagement match domain_sources. FAQ 5 arithmetic corrected in review (one person in 30 is about 3 points, so two people is about 7).

distinct.evidence: Watch-list followed: FAQ 10 separates satisfaction ("whether the job meets people's needs") from engagement ("how committed they are"); tabs (nursing, school district, remote vs office) are this page's own.

faq.evidence: 10 items, each answered in sentence one ("Good ones ask about one thing at a time.", "Only when nothing stored beside an answer points back to a person.", "There is no universal pass mark"); hub link in item 2.

images.evidence: 287 of 350 = 82%, Pay 118/287 = 41%; 4 West night 6 of 16 = 38% emailed to the nurse manager; Cedar Primary 4 answers shows n/a; remote equipment 43% lowest with the IT request list. All drawn numbers add up.
